full_judgment: 12. Possession of original scripts and admission of the Respondent No. 2 to have executed share transfer instruments (in three sets), her signatures duly verified, and submitting declaration to BSEC leads this court to draw the natural interference that the Respondent No. 2 have done all these things only after receiving entire consideration for 20,000 shares. Mere non-existence of receipt can lead to another presumption that she did not give the receipt to evade taxation or for similar reason in as much as it was her duty to give the receipt or to refuse doing the above recorded deeds and things if she had not received the consideration. Raising such a plea as defence after filing a petition under section 43, is apparently false, nullified by the facts and circumstances of this case and is malafide, in my considered view.
